"Carlos Fonseca" explained to him, the original had been lost, so they decided to look for the one closest to the sequence —taken a second before or after the other— to replace it. "It was almost the same, only in this one I had a lost look," Carlos revealed that although NLP (natural-language processing) models are capable of incredible feats, their abilities are very much limited by the amount of context they receive. This limitation could cause difficulties for researchers who hope to use them to do things such as analyze ancient languages. In some cases, there are no contexts at all to provide.

Sarah Waters' novel "Fingersmith" also plays with the concept of context in its structure. Waters uses the first line of the novel to signify where she begins, cycling the story. Even the novel's language bridges this divide. Waters often employs the word "queer" to describe the unusual or remarkable, instead of its post-1922 connotations.
